newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 28.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** Former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress says party chief G.K. Moopanar to decide about joining Prime Minister I.K. Gujral's government in two days
** India's annual inflation as measured by the wholesale price index falls to 6.64 percent in the week ended April 12 from 6.99 percent in the previous week
** Communist parties in the ruling 15-party coalition government plan to review cuts in personal taxes, the Economic Times newspaper reports
** The Indian rupee's gains against the dollar and the devaluation of local currencies by neighbouring nations will worsen a slowdown in India's exports, bankers and businessmen say
** Weak world gold prices seen boosting demand in the Indian subcontinent, the world's biggest gold consuming nation
** Indian stocks expected to rise selectively on easier liquidity and improved political situation, dealers say
** Bombay exchange's benchmark index surged 129.05 points, or 3.5 percent, to 3,825.57 last week
** Foreign funds pulling out from most Asian markets but Merrill Lynch bucks trend saying they pumping money into India from Latin America
"India appears to offer some of the best value
regionally," Merrill Lynch said in a strategy report
** Company debentures command premia and yields fall, as declining interest rates, easier liquidity push up demand
** The Delhi Stock Exchange will replace 18 existing shares with more actively-traded stocks in a major recast of its 33-share benchmark index on Monday
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.765/775 to the dollar on Monday, seen awaiting month-end demand to give direction
